solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cold soup I'd prepared for old vegetarian

indicators.note: soup that is prepared has been made up, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone makes chilled soup for an elderly vegetarian guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old vegetarian' sounds like an aged person, but it is a long-extinct plant-eating dinosaur.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-necked dinosaur was a herbivore that died out millions of years ago.

clue.text: Remove insects from grand university flower patch being planted up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read bottom to top

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
a bed is a patch for flowers

explanation.surface: A gardener clears bugs out of a university flowerbed being planted.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a place of bugs, literally insects, is the plain sense here.

clue.text: Heavy metal venue

definitions.meaning: the London ... is a famous West End theatre

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a dense chemical element and the famous London theatre.

clue.text: Where southpaw may prefer a broken finger, alternatively

definitions.text: Where southpaw may prefer a broken finger
definitions.meaning: a left-hander would rather the injury were on the right, not the hand used most
used to introduce a contrasting point

explanation.surface: A left-hander would sooner have a broken finger elsewhere, or perhaps not.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces an opposing point, just as alternatively does.

clue.text: Expelling son disrupting excursion

indicators.note: the son breaks into the excursion, sitting inside it

parts.note: an outing is an excursion

explanation.surface: A misbehaving boy ruins a family trip and gets sent home.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousting someone is forcing them out, expelling them.

clue.text: UK and USA's first redesign of Elle — it may feature a G-string

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of USA is taken
redesigning the magazine name rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: British and American editions team up to relaunch Elle magazine, featuring skimpy lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'G-string' looks like lingerie, but it is a string tuned to G on a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This small four-stringed Hawaiian instrument is usually tuned G-C-E-A.

clue.text: Electric Light Orchestra's final minute cutting record

indicators.note: the record is cut into by the other pieces, which go into its middle

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: the last letter of the word Orchestra is taken

explanation.surface: A tale about the band ELO, its last minute and a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Electric Light Orchestra' reads as the band's name, but the definition is just 'Electric Light'; the 's is part of the possessive, and 'final' takes A, the last letter of Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp is a device that gives electric light, so it stands for the phrase.

clue.text: Dispute over EU subsidies being cut in half

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: halving the word leaves its first three letters

parts.note: grants are subsidies

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over EU subsidies being halved.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue is to quarrel, to dispute a point.

clue.text: Vessel with innovative remote device for measuring water uptake

parts.note: a pot is a vessel

indicators.note: innovative means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vessel paired with a clever remote gadget for monitoring water.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists use this instrument to measure how fast a plant shoot draws up water.

clue.text: Around middle of March, company twice lied about rents put on waterworks

indicators.note: the company pieces go around the middle letter of March
the company abbreviation appears twice
the middle letter of the word March is taken
about signals the letters are shuffled around

parts.note: taken as written
rents and tears are rips in cloth

explanation.surface: In mid-March a company lied about rents again, sparking tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' sets R inside the doubled CO after its first C. 'waterworks' is British slang for crying, so putting it on is fake weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: False sobbing, shown for effect, is the insincere weeping meant by putting on the waterworks.

clue.text: Fungus: see tons by us on tree trunk

indicators.note: in a down-style reading, the tons and us come on, that is after, the tree trunk
by means beside, so the us piece sits next to the tons piece

parts.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A field guide entry pointing the reader to a fungus growing on a tree trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link in the style of a cross-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: This genus of mushrooms includes the cep or porcini, a prized edible fungus.

clue.text: Honest old maid with sort of milk round

indicators.note: the milk goes round, enclosing the old maid

parts.note: UHT is ultra-heat-treated, long-life milk
a prig is a prim, priggish person, as an old maid is stereotyped

explanation.surface: An honest spinster carries some milk on a delivery round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a milk round, a British door-to-door milk delivery, but it signals enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is honourable and principled, which is honest.

clue.text: Fruit supplier given pear with a difference

indicators.note: something done with a difference is altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone supplying fruit hands over a pear that is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' looks like a link word, but its letters are part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A vine bearing grapes supplies fruit, so the description fits.

clue.text: Rich food is stuff packed with energy

indicators.note: the stuff piece is packed with, so holds, the energy piece

parts.note: to cram is to stuff
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dietary note that rich food is full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairy fat skimmed from milk is a rich food.

clue.text: Pass out roly-poly with cool filling

indicators.note: the cool piece fills, so goes inside, the roly-poly piece

parts.note: roly-poly means plump, fat
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: Someone collapses after eating a roly-poly pudding with a cold filling.
explanation.walkthrough: Roly-poly is also a British rolled jam pudding, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: To swoon or lose consciousness briefly is to pass out.

clue.text: Apparent worth of portrait?

parts.note: worth judged by appearances, and wryly what a painted likeness of someone's features is worth

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means worth as it first appears; a portrait's value would literally lie in the visage shown.

clue.text: Most eager welcome outside fizzles out

indicators.note: the welcome goes outside, around, the fizzles out piece

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
dies means fizzles out, peters away

explanation.surface: The keenest reception outdoors gradually loses its spark.
explanation.definitionFit: Being greediest means having the strongest appetite or desire, the most eager.

clue.text: Rent our agency's accommodating escorts

indicators.note: the words accommodate, house within them, the letters needed

explanation.surface: A rental agency puts up escorts for clients.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue of attendants is a group of escorts.

clue.text: Able to manage carrying medium-sized camping gear

indicators.note: the manage piece carries, holds within it, the medium-sized piece

parts.note: to cope is to manage
M is the clothing size label for medium
a tent is a piece of camping gear

explanation.surface: Someone capable of handling a mid-sized load of camping equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Able to manage' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Able'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Competent and able both mean having the skill needed.

clue.text: Eastern end of green space raised and prepared for fencing

indicators.note: the end letter of the green space piece is the one that moves
in a down clue, raised means lifted to the top, the front

parts.note: a garden is a green space

explanation.surface: A gardener lifts the eastern end of a green and readies the fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of ... raised' takes the N of GARDEN to its front, giving NGARDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencers call out this French phrase as a warning to take a guard position, ready to fight.

clue.text: Speaker's wife in wobble near the edge

indicators.note: the wife goes in the wobble piece

parts.note: to teeter is to wobble unsteadily, as on a brink

explanation.surface: The Speaker's wife totters dangerously close to a ledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker's' is Speaker is, the 's a link; the Speaker is a loudspeaker unit, not a parliamentary chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A small loudspeaker for high frequencies is the kind of speaker named.

clue.text: After martyred bishop, I'm for the chop!

indicators.note: anything for the chop is to be cut out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: Hugh Latimer was a Protestant bishop burned at the stake in 1555
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A martyr's cry: after the bishop, I'm next for execution.
explanation.walkthrough: Latimer, burned at Oxford under Mary I, is famous in English history.
explanation.definitionFit: Later and after both mean following in time, as adverbs.

clue.text: Grouse hiding head in wild plant

indicators.note: hiding its head means the first letter is dropped from view

parts.note: to kvetch is to complain, grouse

explanation.surface: A grouse bird conceals its head among the wild undergrowth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' suggests the game bird, but it is the verb meaning to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: This leguminous climbing plant grows wild in hedges and fields.

clue.text: Mock sporting supporters out loud

indicators.note: out loud means the supporters word is said, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: tees are pegs supporting golf balls

explanation.surface: Fans jeer noisily at the opposition team.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease is to make fun of, to mock.

clue.text: Relative of extinct bird having tail clipped by National Trust

indicators.note: a clipped tail means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: the great auk was a flightless seabird hunted to extinction
NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A rare bird specimen, its tail trimmed by heritage conservators.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's aunt is a family relative.

clue.text: Newspaper taking offence

definitions.meaning: split into two words it names the Financial Times, the British newspaper
a crime that consists of taking someone's property

explanation.surface: A newspaper takes umbrage at something.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense works only with the answer split as THE FT, the pink British business paper; 'taking offence' seems to mean being upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is a crime consisting of taking what is not yours.

clue.text: Large money-making scheme seen in The Apprentice

parts.note: an earner is a scheme that makes money

explanation.surface: A big business venture pitched on the TV show The Apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Apprentice' looks like the TV show title, but only 'Apprentice' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice is a trainee, someone still learning the trade.

clue.text: What baker might make with shortening, each going in stomach

indicators.note: the shortened each piece goes into the stomach piece

parts.note: to stomach something is to take it, tolerate it

indicators.note: shortening a word cuts off its last letter

explanation.surface: A baker uses shortening fat, each portion ending up in the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortening' looks like baking fat, but it signals a cut word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bun with currants, toasted and buttered, is a typical product of a bakery.

clue.text: Journalist contracted with start and finish of eleven PM

parts.note: ED is the usual short form of editor, a journalist

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word eleven are taken

explanation.surface: A reporter signs a deal at the start and end of eleven in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' reads as post meridiem, the evening, but means Prime Minister; Anthony Eden was a British Prime Minister in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden led the British government from 1955 to 1957.

clue.text: Mushrooms in dessert backed after resistance in review

indicators.note: the backed piece comes after the resistance piece

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

indicators.note: backed means the whole assembly is read backwards
the mushrooms go in the dessert

parts.note: a torte is a rich cake served as dessert
ceps are a kind of edible wild mushroom

explanation.surface: A restaurant critique of a mushroom pudding that met some resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses the whole dessert-with-mushrooms assembly, giving ETROSPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking back over past events is reviewing them.
